author: recovery of the unmerged 2026-08-26 Phase C branch (worktree-agent-a2520e5862565ddbf, f81a562 + 9d08106)
decision_rationale: Already concluded an honest negative on 2026-08-26 and re-measured on freshly fetched bars on 2026-09-06/07; the branch was never merged and its trials were never persisted, so this closes a real gap in the project's multiple-testing pool (46 family_keys/1031 trials -> 47/1059). The best of 28 patterns earns Sharpe 0.6296 against a noise benchmark SR0 of 0.9215 -- the best real result does not reach the expected maximum of 28 zero-edge trials. definite_negative at the most lenient rung (the family's own N=28), so the verdict needs no appeal to the pooled rungs.
preregistration_path: data/research_runs/low_frequency_patterns_recovered_2026-09-06.txt section 1 -- NOT a formal pre-registration artifact: this family predates that convention (~2026-09-01). The substantive protection is f81a562's contemporaneous commit message stating patterns were chosen from the literature BEFORE any backtest of this family and explicitly not by mining earlier rounds' per-pattern results, plus a declared MAX_FAMILY_SIZE=40 ceiling and n_trials fixed at the literal family size with no exclusions. No dated pre-run document exists and none was fabricated.

layer_2_mechanism_fidelity.source_citation: George & Hwang, 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', Journal of Finance 59(5), 2004 (best spec); family also cites Bremer & Sweeney 1991, Atkins & Dyl 1990, Grant/Wolf/Yu 2005, Ariel 1987 & 1990, Lakonishok & Smidt 1988, Stivers & Sun 2013, Bollinger 2001, Wilder 1978, Wyckoff 1910, Granville 1963

construction_choices.choice: 28 patterns, each with an a-priori STRUCTURAL reason to trade rarely; n_trials fixed at the literal family size with no post-hoc exclusions and no early stopping
first daily close above the prior 252-day max, 20-day refractory gate, held 10 days, continuation and reversal both tested
construction_choices.source_locus: George & Hwang 2004, Journal of Finance 59(5) -- direction only; see deviations

construction_choices.choice: close-to-close bar returns rather than open-to-close, because multi-day holds must capture overnight P&L
construction_choices.source_locus: momentum.py's existing daily walk-forward convention; disclosed in module docstring

construction_choices.choice: calendar structure treated as known in advance; all price/volume quantities strictly causal, verified by a prefix-invariance test
cost charged at INTRADAY_COST_BPS=5.0 per side (a 10bp round trip) via engine.py:176

deviations.deviation: high252_breakout is a TIME-SERIES event study on a single first-crossing above the prior 252-day max held 10 days; George & Hwang instead use NEARNESS to the 52-week high as a CROSS-SECTIONAL ranking with ~6-month formation and holding periods and long-short deciles.
deviations.reason: This family's declared frequency ceiling excludes a 6-month-hold cross-sectional decile sort. The continuation DIRECTION is theirs; the construction is not. Consequence recorded because it bears on the headline: the best spec is this pattern, and a positive result here would NOT have been a replication of George & Hwang.

deviations.deviation: The bollinger3s_daily reversion leg was originally labelled '(Bollinger's reading)'. Corrected 2026-09-06: Bollinger's own Rule 6 states a band tag is NOT in itself a buy or sell signal.
deviations.reason: Misattribution found by the recovery-time citation audit. The book is now cited for band CONSTRUCTION only. The test is unchanged -- both directions were already tested co-equally, which is the correct treatment for a rule with no author-endorsed direction.

deviations.deviation: Wyckoff (1910) is cited for a 'volume-climax reversal' reading; the 1910 text carries a culmination/exhaustion idea but the formalised volume-climax vocabulary is from Wyckoff's 1930s course material. Wyckoff and Granville were also cited jointly for both readings when each supports only one.
deviations.reason: Overreach found by the citation audit; bounded in the docstring rather than removed, since the exhaustion idea genuinely is in the source.

deviations.deviation: Atkins & Dyl, Grant/Wolf/Yu and Stivers & Sun were cited for their effects' existence without those papers' own finding that the effect is at or below transaction costs (and, for Grant/Wolf/Yu, that the evidence is from index futures rather than equities).
deviations.reason: Systematic omission found by the citation audit, now stated. It cuts toward MORE caution: the prior these sources license is 'real but not obviously tradeable net of costs', which makes this negative less surprising.

layer_2_mechanism_fidelity.independent_reviewer: citation-audit reviewer (separate agent; did not write the module) -- 12/12 works checked against retrieved primary/publisher sources
layer_2_mechanism_fidelity.independent_reviewer_findings: Ten of twelve citations check out exactly on existence, authors, year and journal/publisher; no invented paper, no wrong journal, no wrong year. One real misattribution (Bollinger), one overreach (Wyckoff volume-climax), one missing deviation disclosure (George & Hwang construction), and one systematic omission (three sources' own transaction-cost caveats). All four are recorded in deviations above and corrected in the module docstring; none touches a pattern definition or a number. NOT signed off by the project owner, and not merged to main.

layer_3_regime_conditional.claim_evidence: Every cited source states its effect unconditionally -- a monthly/holiday/expiration-week seasonal, a post-extreme-move reversal, a 52-week-high momentum effect. None claims the effect holds only in a named regime, so no regime-conditional split is called for under CLAUDE.md's conditional rule.
layer_3_regime_conditional.not_applicable_reason: Unconditional claims, so no regime split was pre-declared and none is computed. Recorded separately in layer 4: the 2021-2026 window sees only rate_hike_2022 and misses covid_2020 entirely, which would have sharply qualified a positive result but does not affect this negative.

capacity.method: median ADV across the 284 PHASE_B_UNIVERSE_15MIN tickers (computed from the fetched 15-minute bars, trailing ~1yr) x 1% participation cap x ~21 concurrent names (284 tickers x 7.43% time-in-market, itself 1.87 trades/ticker-yr x 10 hold days / 252). Informational only; no capital is deployed.

regime_coverage.statement: The sample begins in January 2021 and so misses the COVID crash entirely, along with the GFC and dot-com bust; it has seen exactly one stress regime (the 2022 rate-hike cycle). For a family built substantially on calendar seasonality and extreme-move reversal, both of which behave differently in a crisis, that is a material limit on what a positive result could have meant. It does not weaken this negative.
